content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"All three blind responses converge on oil as symbolizing the Holy Spirit—the Spirit's anointing, empowering, and consecrating presence—citing 1 Samuel 16:13, Isaiah 61:1/Luke 4:18, Acts 10:38, Zechariah 4, and Exodus 30. Secondary senses (healing, joy, consecration, abundance, readiness/light) are treated as common but derivative; 'good works' appears only as a minority contextual reading of Matthew 25, and one response notes scholarship resists a universal oil=Spirit equation.","book_summary":"The book defines oil as 'the pressed, tested fruit of the olive — proven works that make light,' and explicitly denies the dominant view: 'not the Spirit.' It builds a chain from Exodus 27:20 (beaten olive oil fuels the perpetual lamp) through Proverbs 21:20 (oil stored in the dwelling of the wise) and Matthew 25 (the wise virgins' oil) to Matthew 5:16, where the light seen by men is expressly 'good works.'","rationale":"The book's entry does not merely refine the consensus; it directly negates it. The consensus's primary meaning across all three responses is the Holy Spirit, and the book says 'not the Spirit,' substituting proven works as the fuel of visible light. While a 'good works' reading of Matthew 25's oil appears in the consensus material, it is listed only as a minority contextual reading of one parable, not as the symbol's primary meaning across Scripture, and never framed as excluding the Spirit interpretation. The book displaces the recognizable common interpretation, so DIVERGENT rather than REFINED or NOVEL.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"The cited chain is inferential: Matthew 5:16 identifies the visible light—not the oil—with good works, so equating the fuel with works conflates cause and output; meanwhile the strongest consensus prooftexts (1 Sam 16:13; Zech 4:6; Acts 10:38; 1 John 2:20,27), where anointing oil is explicitly linked to the Spirit, are left unaddressed by the printed citations, so the negative claim 'not the Spirit' is asserted rather than demonstrated. Additionally, oil in Matt 25:9 can be bought, which cuts multiple ways and does not uniquely favor works.","confidence":"high"}
